#1. Emery and Nagelsmann are top targets if Manchester United sack Carrick

Carrick expected to be in charge for Bournemouth game

Compensation could be obstacle for Aston Villa’s Emery

Unai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann have emerged as leading targets to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United’s head coach should the board decide on a change after the club’s poorest start to the season since 1986.

Carrick is expected to remain in place for Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth – he is due to hold his pre-game media conference on Friday – but the 45-year-old’s job is in the balance after two wins from 11 games this season.

Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation at Como in the Champions League has focused attention at United on a potential candidate to succeed Carrick should he be removed. Emery and Nagelsmann have admirers at board level.

Emery is contracted to Aston Villa until 2029, and Nagelsmann is unemployed after leaving his position as Germany’s manager in the wake of the team’s last-32 World Cup exit in the summer.

Emery has impressed since taking over Villa in 2022, last season winning the Europa League, the club’s first major trophy since 1996, and finishing fourth, one place behind United.

But Emery earns between £10m and £12m a year, so the compensation package United would have to pay Villa may be a stumbling block. He has also won trophies with Sevilla, Paris Saint-Germain and Villarreal and had a less successful spell with Arsenal.

Nagelsmann has managed Hoffenheim, RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich, with whom he won the Bundesliga in 2022 before being sacked in March 2023. He is highly regarded by United’s head of recruitment, Christopher Vivell.

The 39-year-old Nagelsmann guided Germany to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by the eventual winners, Spain. It is understood Nagelsmann would be interested in an approach from United.

Other potential candidates who may be considered include Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Kieran McKenna. They are out of work after leaving jobs with Napoli, Newcastle and Ipswich respectively. It is understood Fabian Hürzeler is not open to leaving Brighton at this stage.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Bruno Fernandes’s house was the target of a break-in while United’s captain was away with the team at the Como defeat. His family were not at home, it is understood, and the intruders were inside for less than five minutes before the police arrived.

The club is supporting Fernandes and his family and have asked for privacy regarding what it said was a difficult time.

Meanwhile, the 32-year-old midfielder is not expected to face any disciplinary action for his criticism of Carrick on Wednesday. Fernandes questioned the head coach’s tactics following the Como defeat.

#4. Prepare for supply chain disruption from cyber or climate emergencies, Streeting warns public

Members of the public and businesses need to think more about how they would cope with natural disasters, cyber-attacks or state-sponsored terrorism, the defence secretary has said.

Wes Streeting warned people needed to be more aware of emerging risks facing the UK and make plans to deal with them.

He added that the government was launching a "national resilience conversation" to raise awareness, including advice for households like stocking up on food, bottled water and first aid supplies.

Streeting also said that cyber incidents - like the recently discovered critical security flaw in the programming language which powers much of the internet - will happen "more and more".

Streeting told BBC One's Question Time that the UK is facing a greater threat to the country, "than we have certainly for most, if not all, of my lifetime".

Speaking to an audience at the UK Gun Hall Plant in Telford earlier on Thursday, where it was announced production of tank gun barrels would return to the UK, he spoke of "everyday challenges" facing households.

He pointed to wildfires burning this summer and the flooding that is expected this winter.

Streeting said the public need to be prepared for "increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks" on businesses, or supply chain disruption caused by "hostile state actors or terrorists".

The defence secretary referenced the critical security flaw in the PHP programming language which has left organisations around the world scrambling to update their systems.

In the UK, 32 government services were offline while the potential cyber-security issues were addressed.

"It's not just from foreign states engaged in espionage or sabotage; it's also organised criminals," Streeting told Question Time.

"In this world of AI that we live in... it does also present threats if people are innovating and pushing against conventional [cyber] defences."

The defence secretary on Thursday spoke at the opening of the UK Gun Hall Plant in Telford, Shropshire

The government hopes to improve the UK's preparedness for emergencies, such as those caused by increasingly likely severe weather events and cyber-attacks by hostile states.

Incidents could leave the public without access to everyday services such as mains water, sewage, phones and the internet.

The "Be Ready" campaign encourages households to stock up on supplies to survive for three days, including non-perishable food, bottled water, a torch, sleeping bags, and first aid items.

It also suggests having a FM radio for updates during outages, and writing down the frequencies of any national or local radio stations you use for news.

Asked by a Question Time audience member whether the campaign amounted to scaremongering, Streeting said the government want "people to be alert but not alarmed".

He said that there was not a "specific thing we've got in mind" when putting out the advice.

But, he added that the supplies on the list "might help you through some power cuts, or might also help you through if... your local shop's subject to a cyber-attack and your card isn't working at the till".

Security Minister Dan Jarvis MP said the advice will ensure emergency services can prioritise people who need more support during crises, and hopes it will "improve our resilience as a nation".

It follows on from similar campaigns by European countries, like France, Ireland and the Netherlands, where the advice is a "normal part of everyday life", he added.

Last month Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle said people should prepare for extreme weather as the strongest El NiÃ±o event in a generation develops over the Pacific Ocean.

She said the powerful natural climate phenomenon will lead to "more extreme storms in this country", and that households should stock up on food to be more resilient.

Her comments came as an National Audit Office (NAO) report warned Britain's food supply chain is vulnerable to plant or human disease outbreaks, cyber-attacks and extreme weather.

The NAO said the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra) had not done enough in recent years to improve supply chain resilience, and that UK households are less prepared for emergencies than those in several other countries such as Finland and Sweden.

The government launched its national security strategy last year, which warned that the UK must "actively prepare for the possibility of the UK coming under direct threat, potentially in a wartime scenario".

It said the nation was "in an era in which we face confrontation with those who are threatening security", and referred to Russia's war against Ukraine and "Iranian hostile activity on British soil".

The government said building national resilience meant reducing reliance on others and ensuring UK supply chains and energy security could be maintained "even in times of crisis".

#5. Dream night for Bournemouth - win over Milan a sign of Premier League power

Bournemouth have beaten Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, and now AC Milan in the Europa League

At times, being a Bournemouth fan must feel like living in a simulation.

That was certainly the case on Thursday night as the Cherries beat seven-time continental champions AC Milan 3-0 in only their third-ever European fixture.

Justin Kluivert scored the opener at Vitality Stadium, 31 years after his father, Patrick, scored the winning goal for Ajax against Milan in the Champions League final.

Having seen their club narrowly avoid the jaws of liquidation in 2008, not many Bournemouth fans would have dreamed that famous name would one day appear on their shirts.

"It's mega. In terms of the story of the club it's ridiculous. Someone told me today, 15 years ago today we were 17th in League One, so it's pretty incredible," Bournemouth midfielder Ryan Christie told TNT Sports.

"So many of these fans have been here for this journey so to have nights like this and win as well is special."

To add to the peculiarity of the situation, Milan fielded more English players in their starting XI (three) than the hosts (two).

While the sending off of Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan killed the contest after 27 minutes, Bournemouth were by far the better side up until that point.

In truth, that didn't come as a surprise, even though Bournemouth have won just six points from seven league games this term while Milan are fourth in Serie A.

The three sides they have beaten this season - Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, and now Milan - have all competed in the Champions League inside the past three years.

For them it's a fairytale, but for the rest of Europe, is it a Premier League-induced nightmare?

Five months after a missed Arsenal penalty denied a Premier League clean sweep in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League, is this yet another sign of English club dominance?

Bournemouth sweep aside 10-man Milan in Europa League

English clubs played nine games in Europe this week, losing just once.

In fact, Premier League clubs have lost just four of 26 games played across the three continental competitions so far this season. Manchester United are responsible for two of them.

In the five seasons since the Conference League was introduced, no league has yet won all three, but in three different seasons Premier League clubs have won two of them.

Over the past two seasons, Premier League clubs have played 21 knockout ties against European opposition in the Conference League and Europa League - and won all 21.

The only two ties they have lost have been to other English teams.

But, despite such dominance, the Champions League still remains elusive for most, with only Manchester City lifting the trophy over the past five years.

So, why are English clubs so dominant in Europe's secondary competitions - and why hasn't this transferred to consistent Champions League glory?

Fifteen of last season's 20 Premier League teams featured in the top 30 of Deloitte's 2026 Money List.

It is easy to see why then English clubs appear to be head and shoulders above the rest when it comes to the Europa League and the Conference League.

Premier League clubs earn more than Â£1.37bn per season in television rights, a figure La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 could only match combined.

Brighton are easily the richest club in the Conference League this season, while Bournemouth and Crystal Palace both appear in last season's top 30.

Last season Aston Villa beat Freiburg comfortably in the Europa League final, with a revenue more than double the Germans'.

Crystal Palace won the Conference League with a revenue of almost four times more than Rayo Vallecano, the side they saw off in the final.

In 2025, Tottenham beat Manchester United in the Europa League final. In the Premier League, they finished 17th and 15th respectively.

In 2022-23, West Ham finished 14th and won the Conference League.

All the evidence points to the Premier League's collective strength. Take away Europe's richest and England dominates.

The summer transfer window was further evidence of Europe's struggles against the Premier League, with the latter again setting a new transfer spend record of Â£3.49bn to dwarf their rival leagues.

Of the 20 most expensive transfers completed in the summer only six were not to clubs in the English top flight.

You now have Premier League clubs - away from the traditional big six - beating other top European sides to signings.

Premier League wages are generally higher and the league is increasingly seen as the place to be for a lot of European talent.

"With the exception of some of the global brands within football, and I think you'd look at Real Madrid, Barcelona, PSG and Bayern Munich, the Premier League can outspend anyone and everyone," football finance expert Kieran Maguire said in August.

"A significant proportion of overseas players are now choosing to play in England than elsewhere in Europe because of the wages on offer."

Despite the success of Premier League sides in the Europa League and Conference League, the Champions League is a harder nut to crack.

While Barcelona, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich all lost to English teams in last season's elongated Champions League league stage, it has been a very different story when it really mattered.

Over the past two campaigns, eight of nine English teams have been knocked out by one of the Deloitte Money League's big four, according to the last report produced in January 2026.

Chelsea, Manchester City, Newcastle and Liverpool were eliminated by an aggregate score of 25-6 last season.

No English club appeared in the top four of Deloitte's Money List, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris St-Germain leading the way. Three of those have won the Champions League five times between them in the last seven years.

English clubs are certainly very much in the mix for the Champions League, with Arsenal losing last season's final on penalties and Manchester City winning in 2023.

But, with just one English club in the past three finals, the Premier League elite are yet to take their European domination to the very top.

Come May, it could well be Bournemouth, Brighton, Crystal Palace or Sunderland leading the English charge in Europe.

#8. Trump tells Iowa rally he expects Ilhan Omar's resignation if she was sworn into Congress with fake name: 'Don't think it's looking too good'

By STEPHEN M. LEPORE, US SENIOR REPORTER and NIKKI SCHWAB, CHIEF CAMPAIGN CORRESPONDENT

Published: 23:58 BST, 22 October 2026 | Updated: 02:59 BST, 23 October 2026

President Donald Trump escalated his attacks on Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar at his Iowa rally Thursday night, alleging she was sworn into Congress using a 'fake name.'

A new name for the Minnesota Democrat was revealed in a Department of Justice filing, with Omar, 44, referred to as 'Ilhan Nur Said Elmi.'

On his Sioux City rally stage, Trump read the new name to the crowd.

'Because she used a fake name to be sworn in, I assume she must immediately have to resign from Congress,' the President claimed.

He called down to House Speaker Mike Johnson, who was in the audience, to get some feedback. The crowd responded to Trump's claims with a 'lock her up!' chant.

'So please inform our great Speaker of the House of Representatives... that the Democrat Party has just conceded her seat,' Trump said. 'I don't think it's looking too good. Republicans have just picked up a seat in the House,' he chuckled.

Trump also, again, alleged that Omar had once married her brother.

'And the last name is, incredibly, also the exact last name as her brother ... the person that they say she married and had children with,' Trump said. 'Are you allowed to do that?' he asked supporters.

President Donald Trump revealed what he said was Representative Ilhan Omar's 'fake name' during a rally in Sioux City, Iowa, and suggested that disqualified her from serving in Congress

President Donald Trump also reveled in an answer that Representative Ilhan Omar (pictured) gave in an interview with MSNOW's Chris Hayes, that 'not to my knowledge' was she ever married to her brother

A spokesperson for Omar did not immediately respond to the Daily Mail's request for comment.

At the rally and earlier at the White House, the President reveled in an awkward answer the Minnesota Democrat gave to MSNOW's Chris Hayes when asked if she had ever married her sibling.

'Well, if you asked me that same question about, let's say, my sister, I would say "no." She said "not to my knowledge." That tells you a lot right there,' Trump told the press gathered on the South Lawn.

On October 12, Omar had federal agents descend on her residence in Washington, DC, as part of a criminal fraud investigation into the Democrat's immigration paperwork.

Omar has characterized the investigation as being politically motivated.

Trump admitted he's 'never been a big fan of hers' and advised everyone to 'see how it works out' with the investigation.

He reiterated, however, that 'that statement tells you a lot.'

Donald Trump believes Ilhan Omar spoke loud and clear when she said she answered 'not to my knowledge' after being asked if she'd married her brother

The Democrat dismissed the long-running accusations as 'insane' and blamed right-wing influencers for spreading the conspiracy theories.

Hayes pressed her on whether there was even the slightest possibility that she was related to her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi.

'You were not related to him at all? There's not a weird kernel of truth...' Hayes said.

The unusual exchange came during Omar's first major interview since Homeland Security Investigations seized phones, computers and other personal belongings from her home.

Hayes introduced the sensitive subject by acknowledging the extraordinary nature of the accusations, which President Donald Trump and other political opponents have repeatedly amplified.

'There are right wing people who believe that this man was your brother. You have called it a disgusting lie,' Hayes told the congresswoman.

'Who was this man that was your husband? When did they start saying that he was your brother? Why?' referring to her former husband.

Trump, who has long feuded with Omar, found it strange that the leftist phrased it that way when asked by the press outside the White House Thursday

Omar married Ahmed Nur Said Elmi in 2009. They divorced in 2017. She has denied claims he is her brother

Omar claimed the allegations originated on a Somali blog before being picked up by conservative activists in Minneapolis.

'It started with the Somali blog. I don't know if it still exists, but somebody put in there that, you know, that he had to have been my brother or something to that effect. And right wing conspiracy theorists in Minneapolis got a hold of it,' she explained.

'And they just kind of went and found random people who were like, she introduced us. She introduced him to us and said he was her brother, which is, you know, insane. I mean, I don't know those people that they talk about.'

Hayes then pressed the congresswoman on whether there was any truth to the allegations.

Omar accused her critics of finding supposed witnesses who claimed she had introduced Elmi as her sibling.

'They just kind of went and found random people who were like, "She introduced us. She introduced him to us and said he was her brother," which is, you know, insane.'

Omar insisted she did not recognize the individuals making those claims.

There is no established evidence that Elmi is Omar's brother, and the congresswoman has consistently denied the allegation.

Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar has delivered a bizarrely worded response to explosive allegations that she married her own brother to commit immigration fraud

Homeland Security Investigations police search the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) on October 12  in Washington, DC as part of an ongoing criminal investigation

The interview also provided Omar's most detailed account yet of the dramatic federal search that has placed her citizenship and personal affairs under intense scrutiny.

She claimed approximately 15 to 25 agents arrived at her residence at 6am, pounding on doors while she and her family were asleep.

'I only had two and a half hours of sleep when they came, you know, pounding on the doors,' she recalled.

Omar said she initially feared an emergency was unfolding outside.

'I thought something was on fire. I thought something was happening to the neighbors,' she explained.

The congresswoman said agents spent between four and five hours searching the property, eventually removing 17 items, including several phones, notebooks, a vintage camera and a Somali language book.

She described the operation as 'intrusive but polite,' acknowledging that agents treated her belongings carefully and even folded some of her clothes.

Nevertheless, she accused the Trump administration of orchestrating an intimidating spectacle designed to satisfy the president's supporters.

'They had to do something, I believe, to say, hey, look, we raided her house,' she alleged.

Federal investigators are examining possible immigration fraud, with the Minnesota US Attorney's Office investigating whether false statements were made in immigration documents concerning Omar's birth date.

Investigators have issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas, including some involving Omar's relatives.

The congresswoman maintains that she legally obtained American citizenship at 17 through her father, Nur Omar Mohamed, who became a naturalized citizen in 2000.

She suggested investigators were now focusing on documents completed by her late father, who can no longer defend himself.

'It's also very convenient because my dad is no longer alive,' Omar told Hayes. 'So it's another thing they can drag on forever.'

Trump has publicly suggested Omar could face imprisonment if investigators establish that she committed immigration fraud.

'She could go to jail,' the president said on Tuesday. 'They keep talking about deportation.'

Omar, however, insisted she had committed no wrongdoing and accused the administration of pursuing a politically motivated campaign against her.

She also addressed separate questions surrounding her family's finances after congressional disclosure documents appeared to value business interests connected to her husband, Tim Mynett, at approximately $30 million.

Omar has fiercely denied allegations of immigration fraud, accusing the Trump administration of pursuing a politically motivated investigation against her

That figure was subsequently revised substantially downward, with Hayes saying liabilities reduced the reported valuation to around $20,000.

Omar rejected suggestions that she was secretly wealthy, portraying herself as an ordinary working American struggling with everyday expenses.

'I mean, it's, you know, working, working class, I guess, like paycheck to paycheck still,' she said.

'We've got four kids. And, you know, we live, I think, like a basic life.'

She pointed to the family's modest vehicle as evidence.

'I have a Toyota Camry that's from 2016. It's our only car. I rent my DC place and my Minneapolis place.'

Omar also revealed that she intends to leave her Washington residence after its address became public following the search.

Citing the death threats she regularly receives, she said remaining at the property would endanger her family's privacy and security.

'I can't continue to live there,' she declared.

Despite the mounting legal and political pressure, Omar insisted she would not be driven out of Congress.

She claimed the president's ultimate objective was to force her from public office, arguing that her opponents resented someone of her background and faith holding political power.

'I think that's ultimately the thing that they want,' she said.

Carrick is under increasing pressure after two wins in Man United's first 11 matches of the season

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There is growing doubt over the future of Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick after his team's miserable 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Man United have now played 11 matches in all competitions since Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis, having steered them back into the Champions League with a fine run of form in the Premier League in the second half of last season.

They have won just one each in the league and in Europe, beating Ipswich Town and Sabah to offer only the briefest of respite from a dreadful start to the 2026/27 season and Carrick's tenure.

With captain Bruno Fernandes openly challenging his tactics and Carrick moving to divert some of the blame to his players, the head coach's days would appear to be numbered.

Indeed, reports in Italy indicate that talks between the United hierarchy and one possible successor for the 45-year-old former England midfielder have already progressed in a positive manner.

Former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Antonio Conte is among the favourites to replace Carrick as the next permanent Manchester United manager, and La Repubblica claims that the wheels are already in motion.

"Talks with Conte continued late Wednesday evening: the manager opened up about the possibility of returning to the Premier League, but has set specific conditions," reports the Italian daily newspaper.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"He is asking for carte blanche on the transfer market and the ability to choose the players who will support him in his new adventure. He wants to influence the team’s construction, identify players who are key to his game, and have trusted collaborators at his side.

"In the next few hours, the owners will evaluate the demands, a crucial step in determining whether the dialogue can develop into a concrete negotiation. There has been an opening, but an agreement hasn’t yet been reached."

Conte is reported to be demanding control over United's transfers. Jason Wilcox might have a thing or two to say about that but his standing inside the club was revealed to be less than stellar by last week's critical comments from United defender Lisandro Martinez.

Conte has Premier League experience and a league title to his name. He has won Serie A with Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli, and has a well established track record of turning teams that are less than the sum of their parts into winners in short order.

But the 57-year-old would also have to be regarded as a relatively short-term option. He has managed four clubs for two years each in the last decade, which seems to make him a risky appointment for any outfit willing to hand over the level of influence he is understood to be pushing.

Conte is reported to be in contact with United but the favourite to succeed Carrick is former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe, who has tended to stick around longer at clubs with lower expectations than those he'd face at Old Trafford.

Julian Nagelsmann, who had managed both Germany and Bayern Munich but is also currently out of work, is also currently listed at shorter odds than Conte.

Chris is a Warwickshire-based freelance football writer specialising in West Midlands football, the Premier League, the EFL and the J.League. He is the author of the High Protein Beef Paste football newsletter and owner of Aston Villa Review. He supports Coventry Sphinx.

#11. Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends

After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou, the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal, while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh

Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST

It was five months ago but it feels a lot longer. When these two sides met in May to finish the season, the contest doubled as Pep Guardiola’s leaving party after 10 years in the job and twice as many trophies, an era now laden with asterisks. It must be surreal for Aston Villa supporters, too. Their 2-1 victory at the Etihad Stadium, inspired by two goals from Ollie Watkins to complete a league double over City, came only four days after their Europa League triumph in Istanbul, where Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Emi Buendía were the scorers. Buendía is the only one left in claret and blue as Unai Emery builds a new side, one that has picked up in form after a single point from their first four league games. City, meanwhile, are thriving on the pitch: victory would make them just the third side to win their first eight games of a Premier League season. Taha Hashim

Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST

Max Dowman became the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history with his dazzling solo strike against Everton at the Emirates in March. But the supremely talented 16-year-old has found opportunities limited this season. Dowman has played only nine minutes in the Premier League despite scoring twice against Ipswich in the Carabao Cup last month as Arsenal have tried to protect their rising star. Yet the suspected quad muscle injury suffered by Bukayo Saka in Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich means Mikel Arteta is short of attacking options. With David Moyes’s side back in north London, it could be the perfect chance for Dowman to step up in his favoured position on the right flank. Ed Aarons

Coventry and Fulham have only met twice in the English top flight – back in 1967-68, when the promoted Sky Blues took a single point from two meetings, but stayed up by a point while Fulham went down. It is too early to call Saturday’s game a six-pointer in the relegation battle, but the two teams sit either side of the dreaded dotted line after shaky starts. Coventry have shown glimpses of their Championship swagger, particularly in the 4-1 rout of Newcastle, but Frank Lampard wants his players to start thinking like a Premier League team. “I can’t keep applauding the players, believing they deserve to be here,” the Coventry manager said. “Now we have to get over that. We can’t be too soft.” Sunderland, Crystal Palace and Ipswich all visit the CBS Arena in the coming weeks, so there is an opportunity to consolidate. Fulham were linked with Lampard in the summer, and questions remain over whether Álvaro Arbeloa is pragmatic or flexible enough to succeed. Will these sides meet in the Premier League again next season? The jury is out. NM

Tottenham’s recent record against Chelsea is miserable. They are on a six-match losing streak against their London rivals and have collected a paltry two points at Stamford Bridge since last winning there in April 2018. Tottenham finally have a league win – they beat Coventry 3-1 on Monday – but remain unconvincing. Roberto De Zerbi used a 3-4-2-1 system against Coventry. He had problems in midfield but now has to work out whether to change a winning team. Does he stick with James Maddison after the No 10’s excellent goal against his boyhood club? Spurs still looked short of energy at times. There is an argument to bring back Conor Gallagher’s dynamism, but would that hurt the side’s quality on the ball? Mateus Fernandes is another option but is yet to establish himself since joining from West Ham. Spurs’ approach remains hard to decipher. De Zerbi likes possession, but Chelsea want teams to open up as the Blues have searing pace on the break. Given their history in this fixture it seems Spurs should focus on tightening up. Equally they can’t be passive and need a threat on the break. De Zerbi will be searching for the right balance. Jacob Steinberg

Talk of Brighton achieving Champions League qualification for the first time will gain more credence, even at this early stage, should Fabian Hürzeler’s confident side extend their winning streak to seven matches in all competitions. There have been five clean sheets and 22 goals scored in their six-game winning run and the Premier League’s highest scorers will take encouragement from Liverpool’s defensive problems in the comeback against Villarreal, which were not limited to Virgil van Dijk’s early lapses. Andoni Iraola is yet to savour a first home league win as Liverpool head coach – Anfield has seen only four home wins in 13 league games this year – and he will be wary of Brighton’s various threats. But with Rio Ngumoha electric in the Champions League win, Florian Wirtz improving and Alexander Isak increasingly decisive, the ingredients are in place for another enthralling spectacle. Andy Hunter

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Who can or will lift Manchester United after the latest dismal/embarrassing week? Bruno Fernandes’s abdication of captaincy duties – accusing his manager of being tactically inept – showed what a rabble the team has become under Michael Carrick; and beyond the double footballer of the year, is there another star act who can win a game? Bournemouth will hope to take advantage, register only a second league win of the season, and deepen the misery for their hosts and fans. If his side goes down to the Cherries, Carrick will surely follow: the latest victim of the United circus. Jamie Jackson

Manchester United v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm GMT

It’s been six months since Crystal Palace recorded a clean sheet in the Premier League at Selhurst Park and the pressure will be on Pierre Sage against Newcastle on Sunday. Palace have conceded eight goals in four home league games this season, although they welcome back Axel Disasi from suspension after his reckless red card against Ipswich. The French defender was brought in on loan from Chelsea to add experience but cost Palace in the defeat by the newly-promoted side and had to watch from the sidelines as the Eagles were humiliated against Brighton last weekend. Disasi owes Sage a favour and he will be desperate to make up for his poor start to life in south London. EA

Crystal Palace v Newcastle, Sunday 2pm GMT

Something unusual will happen at the MKM Stadium on Sunday; either Hull City or Brentford will register more than 50% possession. In seven league games, Brentford only had more of the ball in their 1-1 draw at Leeds. The hosts, meanwhile, are comfortably the most possession-averse team in the top flight so far this season, at an average of just over 30%. Both teams have been effective on the break and successful at set-pieces, with three goals apiece from dead balls. This may prove to be a match for the purists, where one clinical moment makes the difference. The Bees head coach, Keith Andrews, will hope it comes from Igor Thiago, yet to recapture the prolific form of last season. “Thiago at the moment is a very marked man, but we’ve got goalscorers throughout the team,” Andrews said of the Brazilian forward, who has scored one goal in seven this season. “Thiago being Thiago wants to score more goals, and he’s certainly not far away.” NM

Nordi Mukiele ranks among Sunderland’s best players and most influential dressing-room figures. Tellingly the former Paris Saint-Germain defender has been scathing about his team’s dismal start to the Premier League campaign and expects a reaction when Leeds visit Wearside on Sunday. “Leeds will be the right moment to show everyone we are not dead,” says Mukiele, well aware that Régis Le Bris’s side start this weekend on the bottom of the table. “We have not been good enough. Right now it’s not us; we are not Sunderland. I believe we can go back to the top. I believe in this team and this staff. We have quality.” Sunderland must use their three league fixtures before the international break – Leeds, Coventry away and Chelsea at home – to remind everyone why they finished seventh last season. Louise Taylor

#16. Fernandes to stay captain as Rooney calls Man Utd players babies

Fernandes criticised Carrick's tactics in the defeat by Como on Wednesday

Bruno Fernandes will remain as Manchester United captain and will not be disciplined for his post-match criticism of Michael Carrick after the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.

The United skipper criticised Carrick's tactics for the game, then said it was up to the United head coach and his backroom team, not the players, to spot any issues and change them.

It was seen by many externally as a challenge to Carrick's authority, just eight days after United defender Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the club's summer recruitment.

Inside Old Trafford, there is sympathy for Fernandes for the position he found himself in.

The Portugal midfielder did 10 post-match interviews in Como, despite being replaced by Joshua Zirkzee midway through the second half.

While there is disappointment at some of his comments, it is acknowledged Fernandes' annoyance was understandable given the manner of the loss, which was one of the worst in United's European history.

It remains to be seen whether Fernandes will be picked for Sunday's Premier League encounter with Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Carrick will be asked about the situation when he holds his pre-game news conference at 13:30 BST on Friday.

Fernandes has home burgled while in Italy with Man Utd

Carrick carrying on but senior Man Utd figures concerned by performances

Wayne Rooney (right) with former Manchester United team-mate Michael Carrick at the club's Carrington training ground

Former Manchester United striker Wayne Rooney said he was in "shock" and "disbelief" at the performance against Como and he is as "worried as I've been for a long time" at the situation at Old Trafford.

And, while he understands the questioning of Carrick, a close personal friend of the former England and United skipper, Rooney also called the players "selfish" and said "they're like babies" in the wake of the controversial comments from both Martinez and Fernandes.

"When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart," Rooney told the United Stand podcast. "That was the start. We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players because they don't want to take responsibility.

"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.

"These players, they're selfish. They don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. If they're not getting what's right for them, they're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves."

Fernandes' form has dipped markedly from last season, when he was named PFA and FWA Player of the Year and broke the Premier League record for assists in a single season.

"He [Fernandes] is putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it," added Rooney.

"If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez and all of them looked at themselves in the mirror, they'll find what's looking back at them is them, and that's not good enough. They need to show more."

Rooney has also called on the Manchester United board to provide clarity on the future of Carrick, who he believes needs to "come out fighting".

Carrick will be in charge for Sunday's visit of Bournemouth despite intense speculation he is on the brink of dismissal following United's worst run of form since 2015-16.

"I was in that situation [at Plymouth and Birmingham City] and I can only say now, looking back and reflecting, if I was in Michael Carrick's position now, I'd come out fighting," said Rooney.

"There's no more Mr Nice Guy. There are certain things you've got to do to protect them players, but you have to come out fighting for yourself because those players will drag you down and it's going to be you who's going to lose your job over it."

#17. Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found

How did AI discover the internet's massive cyber-security risk?

Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.

Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.

Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.

There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.

Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out.

"The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.

She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".

The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.

A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue".

"But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.

Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented".

"It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.

But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.

He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected, external had been received and was being acted on.

Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble?

Cyber-security lecturer Rory Hopcraft told the BBC the government needed to make sure that its own infrastructure was up-to-date.

"Hacking has been around for many years," he said.

"The government are the ones who set the rules for other organisations... they just need to effectively be practising what they're preaching at this point."

Dean Presley, who has a garage in Chepstow, South Wales, told BBC Your Voice he had been unable to properly process MOTs online.

He said his computer system had been down since Wednesday morning, and while he has experienced outages before, they have not lasted this long.

"MOTs can be conducted and they're legal but none of the paperwork and certificates can be printed and they're not on the system," Dean said.

He said this has forced him to write everything on paper documents, leading to delays for customers.

PHP stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor.

It's a programming language which runs on a web server, behind the scenes of a website, and effectively lets you see the sites you visit.

When you go to a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.

It was developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, but still powers lots of platforms today.

PHP has been used across a wide range of platforms including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress â the system behind many websites - as well as to write tools to build web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.

According to cyber-security firm Wiz, external, which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.

And it said the flaws - now coined "php2shell" - were inherent in the language itself, affecting many past versions of it.

The PHP Foundation, the non-profit which maintains the programming language, warned this meant that, under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker would be able to remotely execute code on servers running PHP.

Some large organisations said they had seen a high volume of attempts to breach their systems.

Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, wrote on X, external on Thursday that the company saw "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.

"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he added.

Amazon also says it saw hackers attempt to exploit the flaws, but its websites were operating as normal.

Cyber researchers at Calif and Wiz unearthed the php2shell flaw, theorised by the PHP Foundation in 2024, in part using OpenAI tools

While the impact of the PHP flaw remains to be seen, disruption continued for businesses and organisations after many sites were taken down on Wednesday.

The website of a Dutch agency specialising in cyber-security, Finland's government and parts of Wikipedia, taken temporarily offline, had returned to business as usual by Thursday.

But a number of sites appeared to have been taken offline on Thursday, as operators rushed to check if PHP might be running within their systems or if any patches were required.

In France, telecommunications company Orange also said, external it had suspended access to certain services globally while it deployed security fixes.

According to some cyber-security researchers using scans to check servers at risk of the PHP vulnerability, the rate of organisations implementing patches - but not as quickly as might be hoped globally.

"The window to respond has shrunk dramatically," said Matt Hull, VP of cyber intelligence and response at global cyber security company NCC Group.

"A few years ago, attackers might have taken weeks to exploit a vulnerability. Now, it can be days or hours."

Hull also highlighted the extent of the task facing developers and engineers working to deal with the issue.

"Several days into this incident, security professionals might already be dealing with significant burnout," he said, urging a need to "make time to rest, share the workload and look after each other".

"Resilience depends on people as much as technology."

#18. Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm

This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight.

Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards.

It was certainly an abject return to English soil for Ruben Amorim, who could have been excused in seeing this particular week as the opportunity to prove a point. Amorim may view Bournemouth as kryptonite given they beat his Manchester United side by an identical scoreline at Old Trafford in December 2024. As it happens that is where the Cherries head on Sunday. On this damning evidence the modern version of Milan share more than a few similarities with his former employers.

“A difficult night in every aspect,” Amorim said. It began with a downpour and waves of Bournemouth pressure, an incisive move ending with Justin Kluivert missing his kick and Ben Gannon-Doak’s drive deflecting wide. Milan failed to clear their lines from the resulting corner and were punished when VAR found Koni De Winter had deflected Evanilson’s header wide with his arm. Kluivert converted the spot kick coolly and the die was firmly cast.

Amorim’s attempt to divide the match into two parts, before and after Maignan’s 27th-minute dismissal, cut no ice. Bournemouth’s tempo had been far too much for Milan before that, Maignan saving untidily from Ryan Christie after Yunus Musah’s pocket had been picked. “We just suffocated them, we didn’t give anything to them,” said a satisfied Marco Rose. “The way they did it today was just brilliant from the first minute until the last.”

When Maignan clawed James Hill’s deflected shot wide, everybody on view set up for a left-sided corner. Nobody was prepared for Maignan, who perhaps expected to be manhandling a taller opponent, to shove Tyler Adams in the face as the ball was sent in. It was a moment of supreme idiocy from the captain; the penalty award was inevitable and so, even before confirmation via VAR, was his departure. This time Marcus Tavernier did the honours, beating the replacement keeper Lorenzo Torriani.

Barely half an hour in, the outcome had been settled. Bournemouth could hardly have imagined, in making their “great escape” from the fourth-tier trapdoor in 2009, that they might land in such a position against Italian royalty. Past luminaries looked on from the stands, Harry Redknapp among them, while their polished successors turned the screw down below.

The relentless Gannon-Doak, called “a special player” afterwards by Rose, thrilled and frustrated in equal measure; the substitute Rayan almost set up a goal for Christie with a delightful piece of skill. It was Adli, another replacement, who applied a delicate garnish.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Injury-hit Hearts produced a spirited display in Turkey but ultimately went down to a 2-0 Conference League defeat at the hands of Mohamed Salah-inspired Trabzonspor.

The Scottish side acquitted themselves well amid a hostile atmosphere before going down to Salah’s first-half penalty and a second-half strike from Franculino, laid on by the former Liverpool star (pictured).

The defeat leaves Wouter Vrancken’s side with one point from two matches ahead of their trip to Swiss champions Thun in a fortnight. Their visit had started in painful fashion after left-back Harry Milne suffered a suspected anterior cruciate ligament injury during training.

Brighton drew a rare blank as they were held to a goalless draw by Czech minnows Jablonec. The Premier League’s top scorers, who have scored 23 goals across their first seven matches, misfired badly in the foothills of the Jizera Mountains in northern Czechia.

Brighton head coach Fabian Hürzeler, in his 100th match in charge, made eight changes from that memorable win with only Bart Verbruggen, Olivier Boscagli and Pascal Gross keeping their places. The visitors squandered a host of chances, the best falling to Jack Hinshelwood, Georginio Rutter and Ibrahim Osman, and Jablonec were looking the likelier to score towards the end.

Antonín Rusek almost capitalised on a mistake by Joao Costinha before Verbruggen had to make a spectacular fingertip save to prevent Jiri Slama’s drive from hitting the top corner. Press Association

What a night, then, for a club that knows what it is to gaze into the abyss. “How did we end up here?” asked the public address announcer before kick-off, a question repeated on a banner hoisted by the Steve Fletcher Stand, but it was worth posing in a different sense too. The sizable elephant in the room was how the Premier League’s 15th-placed team could face down one of Serie A’s most decorated institutions, unbeaten domestically this season, and simply sweep them off the park.

In truth nobody could feign too much surprise; certainly not the bookmakers, who deemed Bournemouth the pre-match favourites. Scoffing at Milan’s inadequacy is, up to a point, simply plucking low-hanging fruit. Football’s ecosystem has arrived in a glum place where outwardly fairytale occasions like this are packaged with caveats: even the English top flight’s relative minnows are, through financial and physical power, playing on a different pitch to representatives of leagues once deemed its equals.

For those understandably immersed in the here and now, Rayan came close to a superb fourth. “I’m happy for our fans especially,” Rose said. It is unlikely to be Bournemouth’s last European gala show.

#21. Russell Brand told fans his age range to have sex was '16 to death' as he issued open invite before handpicking women, court hears

By REBECCA CAMBER, CRIME AND SECURITY EDITOR

Published: 20:36 BST, 22 October 2026 | Updated: 02:55 BST, 23 October 2026

Russell Brand told fans that he would be prepared to have sex with anyone from age '16 to death', a court heard on Thursday.

The 51-year-old actor is said to have issued an open invitation at one of his gigs which led to a long line of fans queuing in a foyer where he allegedly handpicked young women for sex.

At the end of a Hammersmith Apollo performance in 2009, the stand-up comic allegedly told the audience: 'If you see me in the foyer and you think, I really fancy him and I'd like to have sex with him, but I can't because it's Russell Brand, you probably can have sex with me – my age range goes from 16 to death.'

In a crude reference, he is said to have warned fans that he intended to give them something other than signed autographs.

Brand allegedly said: 'If I do speak to you and ask you to come to my dressing room. Please know I am not doing that to give you an autograph.

'I will give you an autograph, but it will be on the inside of your uterus.'

Moments after the announcement, Brand, then 33, is said to have selected a 21-year-old and a 19-year-old girl for a 'threesome' in his dressing room.

Days later, the 21-year-old was invited back to Brand's £2.3million London home where he is accused of anally raping her.

Russell Brand told fans that he would be prepared to have sex with anyone from age '16 to death', a court heard on Thursday. Pictured: The comedian arriving on Thursday to court

Brand, seen arriving at Southwark Crown Court, is facing three charges of rape, three sexual assaults and one count of indecent assault against six women between 1999 and 2009

The court heard from Brand's alleged youngest victim, a 21-year-old who claims she was raped in the bedroom of his home in Hampstead, north London

The star is facing three charges of rape, three sexual assaults and one count of indecent assault against six different women between 1999 and 2009.

Southwark Crown Court heard on Thursday how the victim was so traumatised by the attack at Brand's home that she told friends: 'I would not treat a dog the way he treated me.'

The attack caused internal injuries and left her in so much pain she had to sit on a bowl of ice, the court was told.

The victim, who regarded herself as a big fan of Brand, told friends her idol switched from 'charming to violent and cold-hearted'.

One friend said: 'She told me they started to have consensual sex in the bed which turned to anal sex.

'Russell was holding her face down in the pillow.

'She told him "no" multiple times. She told me there was blood on the sheets.

In the days after the attack, one colleague recalled the victim coming into work looking 'terrible' and 'ashen', before she broke down in tears, saying she had been raped by Brand.

When the victim bumped into Brand by chance months later at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, one colleague said: 'Her face was white as a sheet. She was concerned he had tracked her down and was still pursuing her.

'He was becoming increasingly frustrated because she was not responding to him.'

Brand is said to have 'hounded' her with messages.

'He really wanted to see her, to have sex with her, there was crude sexual language in the messaging,' one witness said.

The victim is said to have told Brand: 'You degraded me. You did something I did not want you to do. Leave me alone.'

The alleged victim said she was driven to Brand's three-storey home in Hampstead (pictured) where she claims she was raped

The victim later told her parents about the attack, but she did not go to police as she feared she would not be believed, jurors heard.

Her father recalled: 'She kept saying she had been assaulted. I said to her, "You have been raped. That is rape."

'I drove her to a sexual health clinic at a hospital.'

Her mother also told police: 'He forced anal sex on her and did not stop even when she cried out in pain.'

She went from being a 'bright, bubbly and confident girl' to battling alcoholism and mental health struggles, the court heard.

Later, a 999 call from another victim who has accused Brand of attempting to drag her into a toilet in 2001 was heard in court.

In the call, the MTV worker said: 'I managed to get away, so to speak, but potentially if I had not used my strength it could have been a very different situation with him.

'Nothing did happen, but it could have done had I not torn myself away.

'I did not feel I needed to report it. I was just a bit shaken. I was a little bit shocked by it. It was very strange behaviour.

'I want to share my story as it might help support other investigations and other women.'

#23. Europa League: Celtic lose to Celta after leading, Mateta returns in Palace draw

Sunderland drop points in 1-1 draw but stay unbeaten

VAR rules out Juventus winner in draw with Rennes

Celtic suffered more Europa League pain as Spanish side Celta Vigo came from behind to win 2-1 at Parkhead. After defeats by Ferencvaros and Benfica in their first two league phase fixtures, Martin O’Neill’s side struggled to impose themselves on the visitors who were neat and tidy without really testing Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone.

Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half to thrill the Celtic fans but Spain defender Javi Rodríguez scored twice in three minutes – a header then an unstoppable drive – to stun the home side who could not find a way back.

It was another damaging Euro night for the Scottish champions, knocked out of the Champions League qualifiers by LASK on a 5-4 aggregate after being 4-0 up at one stage earlier in the season.

Celtic’s ultras group, the Green Brigade, boycotted the game in protest at the running of the club, albeit there appeared to be only a couple of hundred empty seats, while 3,000 raucous Celta Vigo fans helped the noise.

Jean-Philippe Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day but Crystal Palace could not capitalise on a Besiktas red card to produce a winner in their 2-2 Europa League draw in Istanbul.

Palace were looking to bounce back from Sunday’s humiliating 5-0 defeat at Brighton, and were the superior side before Wilfred Ndidi opened the scoring for the hosts in first-half stoppage time.

Yéremy Pino drew the sides level six minutes after the restart and Mateta – who had a first-half goal chalked off by the video assistant referee – fired Palace to a first-time lead four minutes later.

Junior Olaitan netted a 73rd-minute equaliser, and Palace could not find a winner after Umit Akdag was sent off for a clumsy 77th-minute challenge on Jørgen Strand Larsen, who was subsequently forced off.

Sunderland’s winning start in the Europa League was ended with a 1-1 draw away to Lech Poznan. The point keeps Sunderland unbeaten in Europe this season after back-to-back victories over AZ Alkmaar and Torreense.

In a thrilling opening Sunderland went in front early through Timur Tutierov, who was making only his third competitive start since arriving at Sunderland’s academy in 2023.

The visitors had opportunities to extend their lead when Malick Fofana hit the post and Nordi Mukiele forced a strong save from Mateusz Lis, but Lech responded in the 70th minute through the substitute Leo Bengtsson’s low strike.

Régis Le Bris made six changes from Sunday’s Premier League defeat to Bournemouth, including a first start of the season for Habib Diarra following his return from injury.

Sunderland took the lead in the second minute when Nilson Angulo pounced on a tame pass from Lis, and the winger crossed into Tutierov in the middle of the box to comfortably nod home for his first Sunderland goal.

Robin Roefs was called into action at the opposite end with a double save to deny Patrik Wålemark and palm away Antoni Kozubal’s header before Diarra charged up the pitch and fired into the side netting.

The hosts had two good chances to level when Pablo Rodríguez blasted just past the post and Daniel Håkans was played through in a one-on-one with Roefs but flicked his shot wide.

Sunderland enjoyed a good spell of possession during which the skipper, Granit Xhaka, had a strike parried away by Lis and the rebound fell to Fofana, who rattled the woodwork. Moments later Dayann Méthalie was denied at the near post by Lis as the visitors pushed for a second goal.

Early in the second half, Fofana cut into the box but could only send his effort over and Poznan looked to strike when Wålemark scuffed a shot wide following a good solo run.

Diarra fired wide for and Angulo’s low strike was scooped up by Lis, who moments later made a great save to tip Mukiele’s shot over the bar.

Bengtsson looked to make an instant impact from the bench when his effort from Wålemark’s cross was sent wide. However, the midfielder made no mistake when next presented with an opportunity as a corner rebounded towards him just inside the area and he fired into the bottom corner with 20 minutes to play.

Poznan almost took the lead moments later when Roefs made a brilliant point-blank stop from Michal Gurgul. Fofana skewed an effort wide as Sunderland looked to restore their advantage and the substitute Chris Rigg’s powerful shot landed on the roof of the net, but the spoils were shared.

Injury-hit Hearts produced a spirited display in Turkey but ultimately went down to a 2-0 Conference League defeat at the hands of Mohamed Salah-inspired Trabzonspor.

The Scottish side acquitted themselves well amid a hostile atmosphere before going down to Salah’s first-half penalty and a second-half strike from Franculino, laid on by the former Liverpool star (pictured).

The defeat leaves Wouter Vrancken’s side with one point from two matches ahead of their trip to Swiss champions Thun in a fortnight. Their visit had started in painful fashion after left-back Harry Milne suffered a suspected anterior cruciate ligament injury during training.

Brighton drew a rare blank as they were held to a goalless draw by Czech minnows Jablonec. The Premier League’s top scorers, who have scored 23 goals across their first seven matches, misfired badly in the foothills of the Jizera Mountains in northern Czechia.

Brighton head coach Fabian Hürzeler, in his 100th match in charge, made eight changes from that memorable win with only Bart Verbruggen, Olivier Boscagli and Pascal Gross keeping their places. The visitors squandered a host of chances, the best falling to Jack Hinshelwood, Georginio Rutter and Ibrahim Osman, and Jablonec were looking the likelier to score towards the end.

Antonín Rusek almost capitalised on a mistake by Joao Costinha before Verbruggen had to make a spectacular fingertip save to prevent Jiri Slama’s drive from hitting the top corner. Press Association

Juventus dropped their first points of the Europa League campaign after coming ⁠from behind to draw 2-2 with visitors Rennes.

Zeki Celik gave Juventus a fifth-minute lead, but ⁠the French side ⁠kept their ​composure and were level 10 minutes later when the Jordan international Musa Al-Taamari finished from close range for ⁠his first goal in the competition.

Rennes then stunned the hosts with a Boulaye Dia penalty two minutes before the ⁠break as the Italians struggled to create chances until Nick Woltemade equalised ​from the spot in the 67th ‌minute.

The Germany forward ‌twice went close to scoring again as Luciano Spalletti’s team upped the ‌pressure, and Juve thought they had won it in the 88th minute when Jhon Lucumí found the net from close range, but his effort was ruled out for offside.

The draw at least spared Juventus a second successive defeat following Sunday’s 3-0 home loss to Lazio ‌in Serie A.

Jonas Hofmann made the most of his surprise start for Bayer Leverkusen, scoring twice in three minutes ​to give the Bundesliga side a 2-0 victory at OFI Crete to go top of the table with their third straight win.

Crete, who stunned Hoffenheim 2-0 in their opening league-phase match, were twice caught napping by Hofmann, ⁠who was added to the side following an injury to ​Martin Terrier. Leverkusen have ​nine points and lead Ferencvaros ​on goal difference after the Hungarian side beat Torreense ​4-1.

#24. O'Neill bemoans marginal moments but are Celtic just not good enough?

Three Europa League games. Three defeats for Celtic. They are 35th of 36 teams in the competition after another European collapse, this time against Celta Vigo.

Only Ararat-Armenia and their inferior goal difference keeps the Scottish champions from propping up the table.

Off the back of Sunday's 7-1 drubbing of Hearts, there was hope Martin O'Neill's team had turned a corner. Instead, the disparity between their domestic dominance and European shortcomings was laid bare once more.

After Mika Baur swept Celtic in front on 47 minutes, they went into their shells and succumbed to a timid 2-1 defeat as Javi Rodriguez struck twice in three minutes.

O'Neill bemoaned refereeing decisions and marginal moments that went against his team, but are Celtic simply "not good enough" to compete in Europe?

That was the verdict of former Scotland attacker James McFadden after a Celtic collapse that is becoming all too familiar.

"The performances at this level haven't been good enough," he said on Sportsound. "Celtic are way short."

Celtic suffer third Europa League defeat in row after Celta Vigo turnaround

Latest Celtic news, analysis and fan views

Celtic looked nailed on for the Champions League this season when they went into a 4-0 aggregate lead against Austrian champions LASK in the play-off round, before shipping five goals in 77 minutes to drop into the Europa League.

O'Neill's side have now lost their last four European matches, conceding 14 goals in the process. Only once before had they done so in the same season - in the 2017-18 Champions League.

"It seems as though Celtic struggle when there's a bit of adversity," McFadden added. "If something goes against them, the confidence drops, their heads drop, they stop playing forward.

"The ball goes back and across, inviting pressure, and there's no way they take the pressure off. That has been a theme."

"A bit of adversity and the lights go out"

After another disappointing night, O'Neill focused on moments that went against his team - a free-kick not given before Celta's equaliser and a Liam Scales header that flicked the top of the bar at 1-0.

"We conceded a free-kick and I thought a second before that we should have had a foul for us," O'Neill said. "They score from the free-kick and it knocks us a little bit. It gave them a bit of momentum.

"I think if [Liam] Scales' header goes in to make it 2-0, we get the three points. We've lost three matches now, remarkably we're still in with a chance [of progressing]. We've got to win here and got to win away from home.

"We take the lead in the game, if we get the second goal we win the match and it changes the whole dynamic. It didn't happen, that's it - we need to try to find a way to win European games."

'We have what we have' - O'Neill speaks after Celta Vigo collapse

Centre-back Liam Scales had by far the most touches of any Celtic player with 121, well ahead of left-back Kieran Tierney (79) and goalkeeper Sam Johnstone (69).

Goalscorer Baur admitted they did not do enough to win and was at a loss when asked what needs to change. "How we played second half, last 30 minutes, we deserved it in the end," Baur said.

When asked if he knew why his team collapsed in such a manner, he responded: "I cannot tell you, sorry.

"It can happen that you get a goal, they can score too, good team - you should then get control back, hold the ball a bit longer to take the momentum away from them. You should break that."

Celtic did not get control back, did not break Celta's momentum and ultimately paid the price.

"I don't think Celtic are good enough, individually and collectively, to take on a team that's eighth in La Liga," former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner said on Sportsound.

"They moved the ball really well and Celtic couldn't get close to them.

"They are not good enough at this level. Celtic are paying big money for some players because the fans are demanding it and then they come in and aren't good enough."

Their next European outing comes on 5 November as they host Besiktas, trying to reverse their continental woes. Whether they can or not is another matter.

'Celtic are just not good enough at this level'

#27. Musk has restored access to Ukraine's Starlink network, Trump says

Watch: Trump says Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access after row

Elon Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access, US President Donald Trump has said after restrictions hampered Kyiv's armed forces.

Trump made the comments after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said connectivity to the military-grade Starshield network, which is provided by Musk's satellite-based Starlink system, had yet to be fully restored.

Musk previously denied he was behind the slowdown, which affects Ukraine's ability to use drones to attack Russia and protect itself from attacks.

Trump refused to be drawn on a report that he had called Musk to ask him to lift restrictions to the service, but when asked about it he said: "Bottom line, he put it back."

The Trump administration previously denied instructing Musk's company to restrict access.

The connectivity restrictions came as Trump put pressure on Zelensky to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, which he has argued have caused prices to rise.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move which has been criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

A Ukrainian soldier using a Starlink satellite internet terminal which connects to thousands of SpaceX satellites

Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield in Ukraine?

Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, depending on what communications are needed.

The networks use 10,000 satellites in low Earth orbit to provide connectivity, particularly in remote areas and battlefields.

Modern warfare often relies on the use of high-speed internet to effectively operate drones.

Earlier on Thursday, Zelensky said the speed of the system used by Ukraine's military had still not been restored fully.

Speaking at a press conference, he said the speed "has not been restored to 400 [km/h; 250mph] yet", adding: "We are working on it."

He continued: "I am waiting to hear from US Secretary of State [Marco] Rubio. He promised to get back to me with information within 48 hours or so."

The Ukrainian president made the comments shortly before the Wall Street Journal, external reported that Trump called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starlink.

The US outlet reported that Trump told Musk he was frustrated the Starlink system's speeds were still capped at around 160km/h, according to officials.

The speed limit made Ukraine's offensive drones and interceptors powerless against Russian attacks.

The journal reported that the system was working more normally on Thursday, shortly after their conversation.

BBC News has not confirmed the Wall Street Journal's report. It has also contacted the White House and SpaceX to ask for an explanation.

Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing on 14 October.

Musk said last week that the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink which Ukraine uses for some of its operation. He said the system was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting it may therefore be behind the restrictions.

The White House has repeatedly said it did not order access to be restricted.

#30. Champions League review: PSG take a hit, Man City’s empty seats and teenage hope for Liverpool

The reigning champions must deal with the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for some time, while fans at Anfield were thrilled by Rio Ngumoha

Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday, but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level.

“Why me?” Kvaratskhelia asked his Instagram followers. The PSG policy of resting players in Ligue 1 to save them for the Champions League failed to protect him. By resting Rodri, Barcelona followed a wider practice among major clubs in European competition of saving stars’ legs for big domestic occasions. Barcelona face Real Madrid this weekend though Lamine Yamal is not being spared; his brilliant goal in Paris made it 10 goals, matched by 10 assists, from 10 matches.

Another heavyweight battle saw Arsenal lose Bukayo Saka to a first-half quad injury in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Declan Rice powered in a late equalizer after Harry Kane had put on a show that included a goal and an assist. Does the Ballon d’Or beckon for Kane? The prediction markets suggest so.

Matching Barcelona’s perfect record this season at home and abroad are Manchester City, who continue to thrive amid infamy. A resurgent Phil Foden scored a hat-trick and new signing Allan impressed. The official crowd for their 5-1 defeat of AEK Athens was 40,402, but it looked smaller, and mockery duly descended on the club. There is mitigation for those who stayed away, including high ticket prices for Champions League matches in tough economic times, and a run of five home matches in 17 days. Still, City remain in the crosshairs, and the empty seats raise eyebrows for a club reporting record revenues. Equally, it is fair to point out that Anfield was not full, either, for Liverpool’s 4-3 defeat of Villarreal.

A clean sweep of wins for Serie A, with three of their clubs scoring four goals. Inter let the side down with their 1-0 defeat of Shakhtar Donetsk. Roma defeated Slovan Bratislava 4-0, and Como beat Manchester United 4-1, but the game of the week came in Naples. Scott McTominay scored twice, his first goals since a procedure on a benign heart arrhythmia as Napoli beat Bodø/Glimt 4-3 for their first win of the group stage. “I still need to find my best form, but I am not far away,” said McTominay.

Liverpool were a mess in the first 30 minutes against Villarreal and it was Rio Ngumoha who led the recovery. The 18-year-old played off the right, supplying two assists with his left foot: the long-term replacement for Mohamed Salah may already be at Anfield. Liverpool have nursed Ngumoha along, though this was his fifth start of the season. “Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo [Salah] last year was obviously massive,” Virgil van Dijk said of the teenager.

With traditional Serie A giants Juventus and Milan in the Europa League, Como are enjoying their first season in the Champions League. If Manchester United were dreadful on Wednesday, Como’s rise hit its highest point yet. The club’s success carries echoes of Brighton and Bournemouth’s ascents, although Como’s is even more remarkable. They were a Serie D club in 2008, and the city is now known for something beyond its glorious scenery. Champions League winner Thierry Henry is among the investors in the club as is Como’s coach, Cesc Fàbregas, although the prime financiers are the Indonesian billionaire Hartono brothers.

Jamestown Analytics, the Brighton owner Tony Bloom’s company, has been consulting Como. Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho and Antonio Conte are the elite coaches Fàbregas played under, and he has forged a high-pressing style against Italian orthodoxy. As United labored, they were swarmed by Como’s worker bees. Real Madrid have a buy-back option for Nico Paz, bought by Como in 2024, and the scorer of two fine goals against United. Argentina’s latest Messi replacement is rather beefier than his country’s idol.

As Como deepened Michael Carrick’s plight, thoughts moved to potential replacements. Fàbregas has been mentioned, though United fans will recall the summer of 2013’s unsuccessful chase for him. Had a deal been done, his midfield partner would have been … Carrick.

Another week, another Manchester United PR crisis. This one involved Carrick hitting back at his players, a rarity in his managerial career. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” Bruno Fernandes said.

Carrick’s riposte: “If you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”
